name: Dipole Antenna
description: A charge driven back and forth along x reaches 0.7 c (c = 1, Minkowski metric) and radiates. The arrows show its Liénard–Wiechert field on a resting test charge (retarded: read on the light cone): close by, the Coulomb field of where the charge was; farther out, the 1/r radiation term, proportional to its acceleration, strongest across the axis of motion and vanishing along it, travelling out at c in bands one wavelength (2πc/ω ≈ 63) apart. The drive comes from the fixed source below (n = 1) and acts only on the charge with q2 = 1. Beyond c·(K − 1)·dt the field would be instantaneous; the view stays inside.
